the polyQ tract is not essential for embryonic development, but is important for the regulation of energy homeostasis and cellular senescence.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the normal polyQ repeat in Htt plays a role in regulating cellular energy metabolism and that a deletion in this repeat can lead to subtle phenotypes in vivo.
the polyQ expansion in the HD gene causes a gain-of-function phenotype, and the polyQ deletion results in a loss of function phenotype, both of which are likely to be related to energy homeostasis.
